description: Cherry leaf spot is a fungal disease affecting cherry trees, especially in humid or rainy regions. It causes small purple or brown spots on leaves that enlarge over time. Severe infections lead to yellowing and premature leaf drop, reducing fruit quality and yield.
symptoms: small purple, brown or tan spots on leaves
irregular or circular lesions across leaf surface
center of spots may dry and fall out creating holes
leaves turn yellow and drop prematurely
cream-colored fungal spore masses on underside of leaves
fruit may develop spots and become soft
infected fruit stems may cause fruit drop
visual_signature: numerous small purple or brown spots on cherry leaves
holes in leaves after tissue falls out
cream-colored spore clusters on leaf underside
disease_cycle: fungus overwinters on fallen infected leaves
wind or rain spreads spores to new leaves
infection occurs whenever leaves remain wet
disease spreads repeatedly during the growing season
damage: reduced fruit yield the following season
management: clean infected plant debris under trees
apply mulch to reduce soil splash
prune trees to improve air circulation
chemical_control: protective fungicide sprays during wet periods
prevention: early fungicide application during rainy seasons
source: University of California Integrated Pest Management
